newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - NZ Business weeklies - May 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - NZ Business weeklies - May 16.

text.p: THE NATIONAL BUSINESS REVIEW

Peters' credibility on the ropes: Act's Richard Prebble's observation, that he was "outraged" by Treasurer Winston Peters' statement that "something we now know did occur didn't occur", itself raised a more general question as to how reliable Peters' statements were. Peters initially denied on radio he had manhandled National MP John Banks. Page 1.

Secret inquiry probes police tender process: The world's leading supplier of emergency 111 software has made an official complaint of serious irregularities during the tender process for the New Zealand Police's new $12 million dispatch system. Page 1.

Whale Watch considers suit after boat tragedy: Whale Watch Kaikoura is considering suing the builder-designer of its illfated inflatable, Urauo, and the government after the damning findings of an accident investigation were finally released this week. Page 3.

No shows from Morgan on Hawaii trip: New Zealand First MP Tukoroirangi Morgan did not show up for some official appointments during his controversial Hawaii sojourn -- a trip that was a mirror image of a visit he took the year before. Page 4.

Casino off in Cooks hotel rescue bid: Sir Howard Morrison's bid to rescue the beleaguered Cook Islands Sheraton Hotel development is still on track, even though the group has been forced to drop plans for a casino. Page 4.

Bradshaw coy over SFO ambitions: Serious Fraud Office acting director David Bradshaw isn't ruling out applying for the director's job once the dust has settled on a major SFO management shakeup. Page 5.

Ministers at odds over competition policy: The Ministers of Energy and Commerce appear to be at odds over competition policy. The International Energy Agency's review of the New Zealand energy sesctor has commended this country's regulatory regime. Page 9.

Big brother bother: Government stunts business growth: Inland Revenue has a bundle of evidence supporting the view that the size of government is inhibiting economic growth, says a Texas-based consultant to the department. Page 9.

Pharmac budgets for up to $3.38m in legal fees: Pharmac general manager David Moore is facing a grilling from MPs over the drug-subsidy agency's rocketing legal costs and souring relations with the pharmaceutical industry. Page 10.

Regulator eyes Internet: Possible breach of Commerce Act being investigated: The Commerce Commission is investigating the controversial Internet domain-name reregistration system after complaints of monopoly abuse and overcharging. Page 12.
SFO turns on Davison: The Serious Fraud Office, shed of its controversial director Charles Sturt, on Thursday sought a judicial review of "some elements" of the wine-box tax inquiry. Page 12.
THE INDEPENDENT BUSINESS WEEKLY

Listeners desert O'Reilly's $139m radio network: When the Tony O'Reilly/Wilson & Horton/Clear Channel Communications consortium stumped up $89 million for Radio New Zealand's 41-station commercial network in April last year, the industry reckoned it had paid too much. Page 1.

Ratepayers pay for Britomart delays: The Auckland City Council is still waiting for resource consents for its controversial $1.5 billion Britomart project. As a result the council has already paid the developers $375,000 in penalty
payments. Page 1.
Taranaki power tests coalition deal: Next month's planned sale of Egmont Electricity is shaping up as a test case for the anti-privatisation clauses of the coalition agreement. Page 1.
Skellerup bond rates rocket: The stock exchange on Thursday sent its third "please explain" notice to Maine Investments after the yield on Skellerup bonds continued to sky-rocket. Page 3.

Ian Wishart sues Metro: Auckland journalist Ian Wishart this week filed defamation proceedings against Australian Consolidated Press, publishers of Metro magazine, over its controversial "Oops, Wrong Winebox" story. Page 3.

Sir Roger renews attack on TVNZ: Former Finance Minister Sir Roger Douglas went to the High Court at Auckland this week in a bid to reactivate his defamation suit against Television New Zealand for its controversial programme "For the Public Good". Page 3.

Gawler Gold loses lustre: The April listing of Australian mining company Gawler Gold and Mineral Exploration NL on the New Zealand stock exchange could not have come at a worse time, says Gawler Gold chairman Robert Annells. Page 4.

Rebels torpedo kiwifruit cartel's flagship, Zespri: Dissident kiwifruit growers say the NZ Kiwifruit Marketing Board proceeded with plans for year-round marketing despite giving court undertakings it would not do so. Page 5.
Crack down on power monopolies: The Commerce Ministry is proposing tough new information disclosure rules aimed at breaking the monopoly power of electricity supply companies. Page 7.
